code/ch10/tma_multicast_cluster.cu:168
TMA multicast GEMM loads the B tile from the transposed location, producing wrong results
CRITICAL
CUDA kernels (ch06–ch12)
Recent commits
found independently by 2 experts
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

The kernel's TMA coordinates are ordered (row, col), but the shared descriptor helper `make_2d_tensor_map` (code/core/common/headers/tma_helpers.cuh:102-106) builds the CUtensorMap with dims={height,width} while cuTensorMapEncodeTiled defines globalDim[0] as the innermost/contiguous dimension and globalStrides[0] as the stride of dimension 1. With B stored row-major [K,N] (ld=N), the encoded map's address function is addr(c0,c1)=base+c0*4+c1*N*4, i.e. c0 is physically the COLUMN index. The kernel passes coords={k_base, tile_n*TILE_N}, so each 128x128 TMA fetch lands B_smem[kk][nn]=B[n_base+kk][k_base+nn] instead of the intended B[k_base+kk][n_base+nn] — a transposed, origin-swapped tile. The multicast GEMM therefore computes C=A·(permuted-Bᵀ): wrong math, and its VERIFY checksum can never match tma_multicast_baseline (whose manual smem loads at tma_multicast_baseline.cu:98 are correct), so the baseline-vs-multicast comparison this series' commits (775b05b16 'Fix SM103 TMA multicast build', f7ec105e0 'Fix TMA multicast shared memory builds') built verify binaries for is broken. The bug also propagates into the new hand-written SM103a PTX path (lines 91-102), which hardcodes the same operand order. It runs cleanly for the square 2048³ default (encode succeeds, all accesses in-bounds), so nothing fails visibly — and per HANDOFF.md ('Latest non-B200 checkpoint') the series was only ever compile-validated in a GPU-less container, never executed. The repo itself contains the correct convention: optimized_flash_attn_tma_micro_pipeline.cu:53-60 defines its own `make_2d_tensor_map_col_row` with dims={width,height}, stride={ld*4}, matching the NVIDIA driver contract, precisely because the shared helper is flipped.

EVIDENCE
tma_multicast_cluster.cu:167-168: `// Coordinates follow the descriptor's dimension order (row, col).` / `const int coords[2] = {k_base, tile_n * TILE_N};` — fed to both `cptx::cp_async_bulk_tensor(...)` (line 178) and the new `issue_tma_multicast_sm103(...)` asm (`"[%0], [%1, {%2, %3}], [%4], %5;"`, lines 91-102). Root cause in tma_helpers.cuh:102-106: `// Tensor map layout is {rows, cols}. We accept width/height inputs in the usual (cols, rows) order and flip them to match the driver API contract.` / `std::uint64_t dims[rank] = {static_cast<std::uint64_t>(height), static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width)};` with `stride[rank-1] = {ld * sizeof(float)}` — contradicted by the driver contract and by the repo's own correct variant, optimized_flash_attn_tma_micro_pipeline.cu:54-57: `std::uint64_t dims[rank] = { static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width), static_cast<std::uint64_t>(height) };`. Kernel consumption at tma_multicast_cluster.cu:207 expects `B_smem[kk][thread_n + j]` = B[k_base+kk][n_base+...].
SUGGESTED FIX

Fix `make_2d_tensor_map` in code/core/common/headers/tma_helpers.cuh to follow the driver contract like the `_col_row` variant: dims={width,height}, box={box_width,box_height} (delete the flip and its comment). In tma_multicast_cluster.cu change the coords to x-then-y: `const int coords[2] = {tile_n * TILE_N, k_base};` (same array feeds both the CCCL wrapper and the SM103a asm path) and correct the '(row, col)' comment. Then audit the helper's other callers (ch07/optimized_tma_bulk_tensor_2d.cu, ch07/optimized_tma_copy.cu, ch07/async_prefetch_2d_demo.cu, core/common/headers/cuda13_demos.cuh) for the same swap, and run tma_multicast_baseline_verify vs tma_multicast_cluster_verify on a B200 to confirm the checksums now agree.

VERIFIER NOTES

All quoted evidence exists verbatim. tma_helpers.cuh:104-107 encodes dims={height,width} with stride[0]=ld*4; per the cuTensorMapEncodeTiled contract (globalDim[0] = innermost/contiguous dim, globalStrides[0] = byte stride of dim 1 — the CUDA guide's row-major example is size={WIDTH,HEIGHT}, stride={WIDTH*elem}), the resulting address function is addr(c0,c1)=base+c0*4+c1*ld*4, i.e. c0 is physically the COLUMN. The helper's line-102 comment asserting the opposite is wrong. With the call site's width=N, height=K, ld=N (tma_multicast_cluster.cu:371-380) and kernel coords={k_base, tile_n*TILE_N} (line 168), each 128x128 fetch lands B_smem[kk][nn]=B[n_base+kk][k_base+nn] instead of B[k_base+kk][n_base+nn] consumed at line 207 — a transposed, origin-swapped tile. The same coords array feeds both the CCCL wrapper (line 178) and the SM103a asm path (lines 91-102), so both are wrong. Nothing compensates: tma_multicast_baseline.cu:93-98 loads B correctly by hand, so the two VERIFY checksums diverge for random inputs. The repo's own make_2d_tensor_map_col_row (optimized_flash_attn_tma_micro_pipeline.cu:43-58) uses the correct dims={width,height} convention, corroborating the flip. The square 2048^3 default runs cleanly (symmetric dims and box, all accesses in-bounds), and per HANDOFF the series was only compile-validated, so the bug is silent. Severity high stands: the baseline-vs-multicast verification this commit series built is broken, and the flipped helper has additional callers (ch07/optimized_tma_copy.cu, ch07/optimized_tma_bulk_tensor_2d.cu, ch07/async_prefetch_2d_demo.cu, core/common/headers/cuda13_demos.cuh, ch10/tma_2d_pipeline_blackwell.cu) that need the same audit.

code/labs/custom_vs_cublas/tcgen05_cluster.cu:211
Pipelined mainloop reuses smem stage without waiting on empty_barrier: TMA overwrites operands still being read by in-flight tcgen05 MMA
CRITICAL
Blackwell / TMA / tcgen05
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

In the 4-stage mainloop, iteration k issues issue_tma(next_s, next_k) with next_s = (k+3)%4 == (k-1)%4, i.e. into the exact stage whose MMA was issued in the previous iteration. tcgen05.mma is asynchronous: the gemm() calls return immediately and the tensor core reads smem_A/smem_B until tcgen05.commit signals the empty barrier via umma_arrive. The code arrives on empty_barrier[curr] (lines 230-231) but NEVER calls wait_barrier on any empty_barrier before re-issuing TMA into that stage, so the cp.async.bulk write can land while the MMA is still reading, silently corrupting the accumulator. This is the lab's incumbent kernel (autotune.py maps "cluster" to matmul_tcgen05_cluster; optimized_tcgen05_matmul.py uses it; bench_dual_cta.py labels it "cluster (incumbent)"), and run_lab.py only validates under --verify. The same never-waited empty_barrier pattern is in tcgen05_no_wait.cu (line 236), tcgen05_no_wait_swizzle.cu, tcgen05_warp_parallel.cu, and experimental/tcgen05_tma_multicast.cu (line 242). The repo's own tcgen05_dual_cta.cu:294 shows the required wait_barrier(storage.empty_barrier[next_s], ...) before reuse.

EVIDENCE
Lines 209-212: "// Issue next TMA first\n    if (next_k < num_k_tiles && elect_one_warp && elect_one_thr) {\n      issue_tma(next_s, next_k);\n    }" and lines 230-231: "uint64_t* empty_ptr = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t*>(&storage.empty_barrier[curr]);\n      cutlass::arch::umma_arrive(empty_ptr);" — grep confirms no wait_barrier(storage.empty_barrier[...]) anywhere in this file.
SUGGESTED FIX

Before issue_tma(next_s, next_k), when next_k >= kStages, add cute::wait_barrier(storage.empty_barrier[next_s], empty_phase[next_s]); empty_phase[next_s] ^= 1; (tracking a per-stage empty phase array), exactly as tcgen05_dual_cta.cu lines 290-295 does. Apply the same fix to tcgen05_no_wait.cu, tcgen05_no_wait_swizzle.cu, tcgen05_warp_parallel.cu, and experimental/tcgen05_tma_multicast.cu.

VERIFIER NOTES

Verified: in iteration k, line 211 issue_tma(next_s=(k+3)%4=(k-1)%4) refills the stage whose MMA was issued in iteration k-1; the only wait in the loop is on full_barrier[curr] (line 215), and grep confirms no wait_barrier(empty_barrier[...]) anywhere in the file — lines 230-231 arrive on it but nothing consumes the phase. tcgen05.mma is async (the file's own mma_barrier/umma_arrive epilogue sync proves the code knows this), so the WAR hazard is real. tcgen05_dual_cta.cu:293-295 implements exactly the missing wait. Pattern reproduced in tcgen05_no_wait.cu (lines 231-236, whose comment admits 'we just trust the pipeline depth and issue unconditionally'), tcgen05_no_wait_swizzle.cu, tcgen05_warp_parallel.cu, and experimental/tcgen05_tma_multicast.cu (lines 241-243). Consumer claims also verified: autotune.py:96 maps 'cluster' to this kernel, optimized_tcgen05_matmul.py defaults to it, bench_dual_cta.py:123 labels it 'cluster (incumbent)'. Critical is fair: silent nondeterministic corruption in the lab's flagship kernel; the race is timing-dependent (TMA fetch latency usually exceeds one k-tile of MMA), which is why validation passes today.

code/labs/nanochat_fullstack/nanochat/engine.py:584
CUDA-graph decode replays a stale KV-cache write position, producing wrong tokens after the first replay
CRITICAL
Co-design / distributed
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

_capture_decode_graph captures one decode step whose KVCache.insert_kv uses host Python ints for the cache slot: 't0, t1 = self.pos, self.pos + T_add; self.kv_cache[layer_idx, 0, :, :, t0:t1] = k' (lines 277-280) and attends over a fixed-length view kv_cache[..., :t1]. Those offsets are baked into the captured kernels. _graph_decode then replays the graph on every subsequent step (line 584), only re-capturing when ids shape/device, mask presence, or cache_gen (which changes only when the cache storage GROWS, line 160) change. self.pos never advances during replay (no Python runs), so every decode step after the first rewrites the SAME cache slot P and attends over the same fixed prefix :P+1. In Engine.generate() (line 1069 path, no token_mask), any run with model.config.use_cuda_graphs=True (e.g. tests/test_engine_smoke.py line 33, benchmark_incremental_optimizations.py '+ use_cuda_graphs' config) silently generates garbage from the second generated token onward, while the benchmark reports it as a speedup.

EVIDENCE
cache_gen = getattr(kv_cache, "cache_gen", None)
        if (not self._graph_shapes_match(ids, attention_mask, token_mask)) or (cache_gen != self._graph_cache_gen):
            self._capture_decode_graph(ids, kv_cache, attention_mask, token_mask)
        self._graph_static_ids.copy_(ids)
        ...
        self._decode_graph.replay()
        return self._graph_output
SUGGESTED FIX

Make the KV write position a device-side tensor that the captured graph reads and increments on-GPU (index_copy_ with a position tensor, incremented by a captured kernel), and make the attention length static (attend over the full preallocated cache with a mask driven by the position tensor). Alternatively, re-capture per position or disable the graph path entirely until the cache is graph-safe; the current cache_gen/shape check is insufficient and must not gate replay correctness.

VERIFIER NOTES

Verified: insert_kv's no-token_mask path (lines 277-282) writes kv_cache[layer,0,:,:,t0:t1] using host ints from self.pos, and returns a fixed :t1 view — both baked into the captured graph. _graph_decode (575-585) re-captures only on shape/device/mask-presence or cache_gen change; cache_gen increments only in _maybe_grow_cache (line 160), and generate() preallocates the decode cache to prompt+max_tokens (line 1033-1034) so it never grows. _decode_graph_disabled is initialized False (366) and never set True anywhere (grep), so nothing rescues the path. self.pos advances only in Python, which does not run during replay — every step after the first rewrites slot P and attends over :P+1. generate() calls _execute_decode(ids, kv_cache_decode) with no token_mask (line 1069) and (B,1) CUDA ids, satisfying the graph gate (588-594). One nit: the parenthetical citing benchmark_incremental_optimizations.py is wrong — that script never builds an Engine (see finding on line 159) — but tests/test_engine_smoke.py line 33 does set use_cuda_graphs=True, and any GPU Engine run with the flag hits the bug. Critical is correct.

code/labs/train_distributed/optimized_zero2_multigpu.py:147
Optimized ZeRO-2 never runs the optimizer: overlap_with_ddp=True makes step() a no-op
CRITICAL
Co-design / distributed
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

The script constructs ZeroRedundancyOptimizer with overlap_with_ddp=True but registers a plain custom comm hook (line 140: ddp_model.register_comm_hook(state=dist.group.WORLD, hook=_reduce_scatter_allgather_hook)) instead of a hook built with torch.distributed.algorithms.ddp_comm_hooks.ddp_zero_hook.hook_with_zero_step. With overlap_with_ddp=True, local-optimizer initialization is deferred until a zero-step hook drives it, and ZeroRedundancyOptimizer.step() (torch 2.8: 'if self._overlap_with_ddp: logger.warning(...); return None') is a warning-only no-op. So every optimizer.step() at line 189 does nothing: parameters are never updated, AdamW math never executes, and 'sharded optimizer states' never even exist. The benchmark then compares against baseline_zero2_multigpu.py, which pays for a full AdamW step every iteration, so the reported 'optimized ZeRO-2' speedup is largely the cost of silently skipping the optimizer, and print_memory_stats reports 'Optimizer states: 0.00 MB' — fake memory savings from an optimizer that was never created. The docstring claim 'overlap reduce-scatter gradients with sharded optimizer states' is false: nothing is sharded and nothing overlaps with an optimizer step.

EVIDENCE
optimizer = ZeroRedundancyOptimizer(
            ddp_model.parameters(),
            overlap_with_ddp=True,
            parameters_as_bucket_view=True,
            **_optimizer_cfg(ddp_model.parameters(), args.learning_rate),
        )
...
            optimizer.step()   # line 189 — no-op when overlap_with_ddp=True
SUGGESTED FIX

Either (a) set overlap_with_ddp=False and keep the manual optimizer.step() (the reduce-scatter+all-gather hook then gives ZeRO-2-style gradient comm with a real sharded-optimizer step), or (b) keep overlap_with_ddp=True but register the hook via torch.distributed.algorithms.ddp_comm_hooks.ddp_zero_hook.hook_with_zero_step(_reduce_scatter_allgather_hook, ddp_model, optimizer) and remove optimizer.step() from the loop. Add an assertion that parameters actually change across steps so the benchmark cannot silently degenerate.

VERIFIER NOTES

All claims check out. Line 140 registers the plain _reduce_scatter_allgather_hook (not a ddp_zero_hook.hook_with_zero_step wrapper); lines 145-150 pass overlap_with_ddp=True. Verified in the installed torch 2.8.0: ZeroRedundancyOptimizer.step() begins 'if self._overlap_with_ddp: logger.warning(...); return None' — a warning-only no-op — and with overlap the local optimizer init is deferred to a zero-step hook that is never wired, so no AdamW state ever exists. optimizer.step() at lines 165 and 189 therefore do nothing and parameters never update. print_memory_stats (training_utils/memory.py:40-47) sums optimizer.state tensors, so it prints 'Optimizer states: 0.00 MB'. The benchmark-vs-baseline speedup claim follows: RS+AG comm is equivalent to allreduce, so the delta is mostly the skipped AdamW step. Critical is correct.

code/setup.sh:1924
setup.sh installs the pinned stable torch==2.9.1+cu130 from the nightly-only cu130 index, so setup always aborts
CRITICAL
Build & CI
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

setup.sh single-sources the torch pin from requirements_latest.txt (line 1809: PYTORCH_TORCH_VERSION="${REQ_TORCH_VERSION}" -> 2.9.1+cu130, a stable release), but the install step resolves against PYTORCH_CU130_INDEX, which is hardcoded to the NIGHTLY channel (line 372). The PyPI extra-index cannot satisfy a +cu130 local-version pin, and the cached-wheel fallback is impossible because line 1785 deletes cached torch manylinux wheels ('find "${PYTORCH_WHEEL_DIR}" ... -name "torch-*-manylinux*.whl" -delete'). pip therefore fails and the script hits 'exit 1' at line 1930 on every clean run — the repo's canonical environment bootstrap cannot complete anywhere. The stale header ('Installing PyTorch nightly 2.10 cu130 stack', line 1916) and code/README.md:138 ('PyTorch 2.10-dev') contradict the actual 2.9.1 pin.

Line 372: PYTORCH_CU130_INDEX_ROOT="https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu130"  |  Line 1924: --index-url "${PYTORCH_CU130_INDEX}" \  |  requirements_latest.txt:104: torch==2.9.1+cu130

Point PYTORCH_CU130_INDEX_ROOT at https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 and PYTORCH_TORCH_FIND_LINKS at https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130/torch/ (or select nightly vs stable by whether the resolved pin contains '.dev'), for both install sites (lines 1923-1931 and 3708-3716); update the banner text and README's '2.10-dev' claim to the pinned 2.9.1+cu130 stack.

All evidence verified: line 372 hardcodes PYTORCH_CU130_INDEX_ROOT to the nightly channel, line 374 points find-links at nightly/cu130/torch/, and lines 1803-1810 single-source PYTORCH_TORCH_VERSION from requirements_latest.txt:104 (torch==2.9.1+cu130, stable). Live check today: the nightly cu130 index carries only torch-2.14.0.dev* wheels (no 2.9.x at all), while the stable index https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130/torch/ has torch-2.9.1+cu130. PyPI as extra-index cannot satisfy a +cu130 local-version pin (PEP 440 requires exact local match). Line 1785 deletes cached torch manylinux wheels, and neither pip_cmd (line 474) nor the install command adds third_party/wheels as find-links, so there is no fallback; the install at 1923-1928 fails and line 1930 exits 1. The TE-rebuild reinstall at 3708-3716 reuses the same broken index pair. The stale banner (line 1915) and README 'PyTorch 2.10-dev' claim also check out. code/ch01/Makefile:41
b200/b300/gb10/gb300 targets cannot change the compile architecture — target-specific ARCH is set after cuda_arch.mk already chose the gencode
HIGH
Build & CI
verified by independent skeptic
PROBLEM

'b200: ARCH=sm_100' is a GNU make target-specific variable, but ../core/common/cuda_arch.mk computes CUDA_ARCH_GENCODE, ARCH_SUFFIX and CUDA_NVCC_ARCH_FLAGS with ':=' at parse time (cuda_arch.mk lines 78-107), before any target-specific value exists. Reproduced with a minimal makefile: the recipe echoes the alias's ARCH while the flags keep the parse-time arch. Concretely, on a B200 host 'make gb300' auto-detects sm_100, compiles -gencode arch=compute_100a into *_sm100 binaries, yet prints 'Building Chapter 1 examples with sm_103' — a silently wrong-arch build with a misleading log. On a GPU-less host the aliases die in cuda_arch.mk's parse-time auto-detect $(error) even though the user explicitly named the architecture.
